title: 信号処理
subtitle: Signal Processing
teachers:
TAKEI Yoshinori
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn the foundations of signal processing, including analog-to-digital conversion.
(2) Understand the basic concepts for digital signals processing, including convolution, Z-transform, sampling theorem, and Fourier analysis.
(3) Acquire the ability to evaluate signals transmitted between linear time-invariant (LTI) systems and to extract the features underlying signals.
advice:
This is a basic course in signal processing for discrete time signals. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1.	Basic concepts of digital signal processing.
2.	Expressing LTI systems with linear convolution.
3.	Expressing discrete time transfer functions using Z-transform and its frequency domain property.
4.	Expressing Fourier series and Fourier transform for continuous and discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem.

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Hitoshi Kiya, Digital Signal Processing (in Japanese), Ohmsha
requiredKnowledge:
Sufficient mathematical calculation skills (especially those covered in Control Engineering I).
Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1)	Calculate convolution, Z-transform, and Fourier series expansion signals from various sampled continuous time signals
(2)	Express the discrete time transfer function and its frequency domain property for discrete LTI systems
(3)	Express the characteristics of the frequency domain of discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem
achievementLevels.standard:
(1)	Calculate convolution, Z-transform, and Fourier series expansion for basic discrete time signals
(2)	Express the discrete time transfer function of discrete LTI systems
(3)	Explain the characteristics of frequency domain of discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem
